Interest costs on global government debt have never been higher:

Gross interest expenditure among OECD countries surged +$180 billion YoY in 2025, to a record $2.24 trillion.

This marks the 4th consecutive annual increase, totaling +$960 billion.

The US accounted for ~65% of the total, at $1.45 trillion, while the EU represented ~18%, or $400 billion.

As a % of global GDP, gross interest costs stood at ~3.2% last year, their 2nd-highest level in at least 20 years.

Meanwhile, OECD countries are estimated to borrow another $18 trillion in 2026, the highest annual total on record.

The global debt crisis is spiraling out of control.

a16z's David George says the real economy has barely begun adopting AI, while the top 1% in one dataset already spend $7,000 per employee per month:

"Part of the thing that we're monitoring, which makes us extremely bullish about AI, is just actual diffusion into the real economy."

"The median company in the US is spending $12 per employee on AI per month. The top 1% of the dataset that we've seen is spending $7,000 per employee on AI per month."

"Not only have we had limited diffusion beyond coding, but if you just look at the shape of who is consuming tokens and actually getting real value out of AI today, we're super early. The most cutting-edge banks are probably doing 1% of headcount cost on AI tools."

"The reason this makes me very bullish is these are the fastest-growing companies we've ever seen, of all time. They're adding more revenue per month than the mega-cap tech companies."

"And yet it's probably on the back of adoption of 10 million users, maybe 20, maybe 30 max. And I think it's going to transform the way we do a lot of work."

@DavidGeorge83

BREAKING: The US Debt-to-GDP ratio is projected to rise to a record 156% in 2050, according to the CBO's latest forecast.

That would mark a +57 percentage point increase from the current ~99%.

At the same time, the Treasury Department estimates the ratio will surge to a massive 213% over the same period, or 57 percentage points higher than the CBO's estimate.

Furthermore, neither estimate includes intragovernmental debt, such as Treasury securities held by Social Security and other federal trust funds.

The worst part?

Both forecasts assume the US avoids a recession during this entire period.

US debt could be heading in a far worse direction than forecasts suggest.

Core CPI rose 0.3% in August, above the 0.2% forecast, and hike odds jumped to 85%. But strip out one line item, a record 5.9% jump in wireless plan prices from AT&T and T-Mobile, and core was exactly 0.2%. In line.

That is a one-time price change from two carriers, not broad inflation.

The Fed is about to hike into a phone plan and call it a win against inflation.

tweets.text:
There are so many factors here, but first and foremost, we should not be looking at this phenomena on the HODL waves (BTC denominated). As Bitcoin gets bigger, ancient, deep dormant, and lost coin continue to compress the Y-axis on supply curves, making it look smaller than it actually is.

We must look at it on the Realised Cap HODL waves (USD denominated), where several such 'spikes' in young coins become visible.

There's a tonne of additional factors including the Coldcard incident, folks moving coins to sell the LukeCashJr fork, and the time-pain capitulation that occurred between June and August. What we ended up with is 'several spikes' spread over a few months, rather than the one event usually associated with an FTX or Dec 2018 style red candle.
